questions.q: Where does a GitHub Actions workflow file live in a repository?
options: A separate GitHub-hosted configuration service outside the repo
.github/workflows/ as a YAML file
sfdx-project.json
A .circleci folder
questions.explain: Workflow files are YAML files inside .github/workflows/; GitHub picks them up automatically the moment they're committed and pushed, with no separate registration step.

questions.q: In the example workflow, why does the runner need actions/setup-node@v4 before installing the Salesforce CLI?
options: Because Node.js is required to check out the repository
Because actions/setup-node@v4 deploys metadata directly
It isn't actually needed and is just decorative
Because the Salesforce CLI ships as an npm package, so the runner needs Node.js installed before npm install --global @salesforce/cli can work
questions.explain: The Salesforce CLI is distributed as an npm package, so a Node.js environment has to exist on the runner before the CLI install step can succeed.

questions.q: What is the difference between a 'uses:' step and a 'run:' step in a GitHub Actions job?
options: 'uses:' invokes a reusable, pre-built action; 'run:' executes a raw shell command directly on the runner
There is no difference, they are interchangeable syntax for the same thing
'run:' can only be used for the first step in a job
'uses:' can only install Node.js
questions.explain: 'uses:' calls a packaged, reusable action like actions/checkout@v4; 'run:' executes an arbitrary shell command, the same kind you'd type on your own machine.

questions.q: Why is actions/checkout@v4 almost always a workflow's first step?
options: Because it installs the Salesforce CLI
Because GitHub requires it to be first by syntax rule
Because without it, the runner is an empty virtual machine with no code on it at all for later steps to use
Because it deletes old workflow runs
questions.explain: A fresh runner starts with nothing on it -- checkout clones the repository so every later step actually has the project's files to work with.

questions.q: Where do you go to watch a workflow run live and read its step-by-step logs?
options: The repository's Actions tab, then into the specific run
The repository's Issues tab
The sfdx-project.json file
A commit message
questions.explain: The Actions tab lists every workflow and every run; clicking into a run shows a live, streaming log of every step, with a red X marking the exact line that failed.
